items.title: Three 15-year-olds plead guilty to beating classmate over WhatsApp messages
items.summary: TANGKAK: Three 15-year-old students pleaded guilty in the magistrate's court today to assaulting a classmate in a bullying incident at a secondary school in Taman Sri Kesang. The three entered their pleas before magistrate Arthana Sarma Rao after the charge was read out. MORE TO COME © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: National Laureate A. Samad Said laid to rest at Bukit Kiara
items.summary: Also present were Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Dr Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and veteran newsman Datuk A. Kadir Jasin. Among those who paid their last respects at the cemetery were DAP veteran Tan Sri Lim Kit Siang, OKU Sentral president Datuk Dr Ras Adiba Mohd Radzi and three National Laureates – Datuk Dr Anwar Ridhwan, Prof Datuk Dr Siti Zainon Ismail and Datuk Dr Zurinah Hassan. Dewan Bahasa dan Pustaka (DBP) director-general Datuk Dr Hazami Jahari and singer and composer Datuk M. Nasir were also present.

items.title: Alliance Bank posts marginal Q2 earnings growth, raises dividend
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd's net profit rose 0.93 per cent to RM208.47 million in the second quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM206.56 million a year ago, as revenue increased 3.56 per cent to RM648.50 million from RM626.23 million. For the first half, net profit increased 12.71 per cent to RM456.78 million from RM405.26 million a year ago, while revenue grew 3.05 per cent to RM1.28 billion from RM1.24 billion. Alliance Bank said its first-half performance was supported by higher net interest income, stronger client-based fee income and lower net credit costs.

items.title: Teacher acquitted in RM65k forged salary slip case
items.summary: KOTA BARU: A teacher was acquitted and discharged by the Sessions Court today over an amended charge of fraudulently using a forged salary slip to obtain a RM65,000 loan six years ago. Judge Dazuki Ali ruled that the prosecution had failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt at the end of the defence case. Lawyer Muhammad Hasif Hasan represented Norzaiza, while Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) deputy public prosecutor Asmah Che Wan appeared for the prosecution in Kelantan.

items.title: Five killed in military helicopter crash in Turkiye
items.summary: ANKARA: Five Turkish Air Force personnel were killed when an AS-532 military helicopter crashed during a training flight in Eskisehir province, central Turkiye, on Tuesday, according to Turkish broadcaster NTV, reported Xinhua. Citing a statement from the Turkish Defence Ministry, NTV said the wreckage had been located and search and rescue operations were under way. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Malaysia's leading index rises 2.2pct in September, signals positive outlook
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's leading index (LI) rose 2.2 per cent year-on-year to 116.0 points in September 2026 from 113.5 points in the same month last year. The Statistics Department said the growth was mainly driven by a 44.1 per cent increase in real imports of basic precious and other non-ferrous metals, alongside an 11.5 per cent rise in real imports of semiconductors. Meanwhile, the coincident index (CI), which measures current economic performance, increased 2.5 per cent year-on-year to 132.4 points in September from 129.2 points a year earlier.

items.title: Anwar yet to accept Loke's resignation, says he is still on leave
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has yet to accept Anthony Loke's resignation as Transport Minister, saying the latter is still on leave. Anwar confirmed that he had met Loke to discuss the matter. "I have not accepted the resignation; he is still on leave," he said when asked about Loke's cabinet status at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre.

items.title: Warisan calls for clearer welfare support for medical officers sent to Sabah
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The Health Ministry should clarify accommodation, allowances and other welfare arrangements for medical officers deployed to Sabah to address the state's shortage of healthcare personnel, said Dr Istefan Koh. Koh said several aspects of the deployment arrangements required clarification, particularly accommodation and allowances. "Will the Sabah Health Department provide accommodation throughout the deployment period?

items.title: UMS gets approval to increase annual medical student intake to 150
items.summary: Its vice-chancellor, Professor Dr Rosalam Sarbatly, said UMS would increase enrolment in phases in line with its clinical training capacity. He said the phased approach would ensure every student received adequate training placements, supervision and opportunities to learn alongside patients across all major disciplines. Rosalam said the university would continue working with the Health Ministry (MOH), through the Sabah State Health Department, to coordinate student placements and supervision at government hospitals and clinics.

items.title: Proton bids farewell to Persona after 19 years
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Proton's Persona sedan has reached the end of the road after 19 years in production, with the final unit handed over to a customer at its 4S dealership, Atiara Johan, in Puchong. The Persona succeeded the Proton Wira and was developed using the Proton Gen-2 platform. Proton Edar sales director Ong Chee Wooi said the Persona had served Malaysian households by offering an affordable sedan with space, comfort and practicality.

items.title: [UPDATED] Police: RMAF pilot in RM4.83mil drug haul acted as coordinator, transporter
items.summary: TUMPAT: A Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) pilot arrested in connection with the seizure of 96.6kg of methamphetamine worth RM4.83 million at the Subang Airbase was a coordinator and transporter for the drug syndicate. Bukit Aman confirmed that the pilot was among 13 people arrested over the seizure. He said police had identified several syndicate members before making the arrests.

items.title: Overseas disaster deaths require stronger international cooperation, says Saifuddin
items.summary: Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said existing procedures for registering ordinary deaths abroad were adequate, but disaster-related cases were more complex as they involved the legal and administrative requirements of the countries concerned. He said Malaysia's domestic mechanisms alone were insufficient to resolve such cases without complying with the procedures of the countries where the disasters occurred. Saifuddin said under the existing mechanism, the National Registration Department (NRD) could issue death certificates within seven working days upon receiving the necessary documentation for ordinary deaths abroad.

items.title: Teacher claims trial to sexual assault charges involving 14-year-old student
items.summary: SEREMBAN: A secondary school teacher in Jelebu pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to two charges involving the sexual assault of a 14-year-old Form Three student and showing him a sexual video. The charge, under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017 (Act 792), read together with Section 16(1), carries a jail term of up to 20 years and whipping upon conviction. The charge, under Section 15(e) of Act 792, read together with Section 16(1), carries a maximum jail term of 10 years, a fine of up to RM20,000, or both.

items.title: #NSTviral: Crocodile sighting in Klang River sparks online buzz [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A crocodile sighting in the Klang River has drawn attention after several people recorded videos of the reptile, which were later shared on social media. "Meet Gorgon (the crocodile) of the Klang River. But there are warning signs along the Klang River from Damansara to Kuala Lumpur," the user wrote.

items.title: Three men remanded four days over assault of 62-year-old man
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: Three men have been remanded for four days from today to assist investigations into the assault of a 62-year-old man following a road accident at Lorong Ikhwan, Jalan Pasir Panjang, on Monday. The remand order, which runs until Saturday, was issued by magistrate Muhammad Amir Zainul Muttaqin Mohd Zamri. Kuala Terengganu police chief Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said the suspects, aged between 39 and 44, were arrested yesterday afternoon.

items.title: Matrix Concepts founder Lee Tian Hock named Property Man of the Year 2026
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Matrix Concepts Holdings Bhd founder and group executive deputy chairman Datuk Seri Lee Tian Hock has been named FIABCI Malaysia Property Man of the Year 2026. The company's flagship development, Bandar Sri Sendayan, additionally won the Master Plan and Township category at the FIABCI Malaysia Property Award 2026. Under his leadership, Matrix Concepts has expanded beyond property development into construction, education, healthcare and hospitality.

items.title: RTS Link fares to be announced in January
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Fares for the Johor Baru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link, covering one-way and return journeys, are expected to be announced in January next year. Johor public works, transport, infrastructure and communications committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh said the fares are still being discussed and reviewed by the relevant parties, including RTS Operations Pte Ltd (RTSO) and the Malaysian and Singapore governments. He said the official fares had yet to be finalised, with the Transport Ministry expected to announce them in January 2027.

items.title: New Mount Kinabalu trail from Kiau to launch on Jan 16
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Climbers will soon enjoy a new Mount Kinabalu trail from Kampung Kiau in Kadamaian, scheduled to launch on Jan 16 next year. Sabah Deputy Chief Minister III Datuk Ewon Benedick said development on the Kadamaian side is a core focus of the Kadamaian Development Master Plan 2020-2035 and is expected to be a new economic catalyst for local residents. "I appreciate Sabah Parks' (TTS) initiative in developing the area's potential, including the new trail from Kiau, Sayap Peak, Minitinduk Gorge, Mount Nungkok and plans in Melangkap.

items.title: IOIPG Reit targets yield growth, acquisitions after RM2bil IPO
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Newly listed IOI Properties Group Real Estate Investment Trust (IOIPG Reit) plans to enhance yields across its retail, hotel and office assets while pursuing acquisitions to strengthen income distributions to unitholders over the next three years. IOIPG Reit Management Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Chris Chong Voon Foo said the trust would focus on improving the performance of its existing portfolio through asset enhancement initiatives, stronger hotel business development and better services for office tenants. On acquisitions, Chong said the Reit would closely monitor the pipeline of properties identified by its sponsor, IOI Properties Group Bhd (IOIPG), in the prospectus.

items.title: Court issues gag order in Shuhaily assault case [WATCH]
items.summary: SEPANG: The magistrate's court has issued a gag order barring parties directly involved in the criminal proceedings against Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain from making public statements on the case until its disposal. The order applies to Shuhaily's nine-member legal team, the prosecution, as well as lawyers Kamal Hisham Ja'afar and Muhammad Nor Tamrin, who represent the two Special Branch policemen allegedly assaulted by Shuhaily. Magistrate Khairatul Animah Jelani granted the application filed by Shuhaily's lawyers yesterday, supported by an affidavit and a certificate of urgency.

items.title: Rubiah: Rural TVET programmes focus on local jobs, better salaries
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Rural and Regional Development Ministry is tailoring its Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) programmes to meet local employment needs. "The ministry emphasises agreements with employers in local industries on skills requirements, placement conditions and salary packages for selected programmes before recruiting TVET trainees. Rubiah said there were more than 300 active collaborations between TVET institutions under the ministry and industry players.

items.title: Marine police foil international smuggling bid, syabu worth RM5.3mil seized, four nabbed
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Marine police foiled an international syabu smuggling attempt off Kedah, seizing narcotics and vehicles worth RM5.36 million following a high-speed chase. Also present were PPM commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Shamsol Kassim and Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Investigation Intelligence commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar. Yusri said checks revealed five white sacks containing 100 gold-coloured plastic packets labelled "VIP 666", filled with 103.798kg of syabu worth RM5,189,900.

items.title: High Court dismisses bid to challenge diesel subsidy removal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court today dismissed a bid by two men to challenge the government's decision to end blanket diesel subsidies in Peninsular Malaysia in June 2024. Judge Datuk Norliza Othman ruled that the decision was a fiscal and economic policy matter that was not amenable to judicial review. She also found that the government's decision to retain diesel subsidies in Sabah, Sarawak and Labuan was reasonable and not arbitrary.

items.title: Malaysian driver held with 300 cartons of untaxed cigarettes in Singapore
items.summary: The 29-year-old was arrested on Nov 16 after Singapore's Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) selected his Malaysia-registered vehicle for enhanced checks. ICA officers discovered the cigarettes concealed in several parts of the vehicle. The driver and seized cigarettes were referred to the Singapore Customs for further investigation, ICA said in a statement.

items.title: [UPDATED] Online fraud costs Malaysians RM7.33bil, 193,000 cases recorded
items.summary: He said mule accounts played a key role in enabling scam syndicates to operate, with 254,546 such accounts detected during the period. Charges were brought against people linked to 137,699 of these mule accounts, he added. Saifuddin said there were six main types of scams: telecommunications scams, e-financial crimes, love scams, e-commerce scams, non-existent loan schemes and non-existent investment schemes.

items.title: Caught: Express bus operator merges six departure slots into one, runs unauthorised routes
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: An express bus operator was caught combining passengers booked for six different departure times onto one bus and carrying passengers on unauthorised routes at Larkin Sentral. The violations were uncovered during a surprise inspection by Johor Road Transport Department (RTD) officers and three Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) officers at the terminal on Nov 23. Johor RTD director Zulkarnain Yasin said the bus was initially spotted moving suspiciously around the terminal before officers stopped it for inspection.

items.title: Johor attracts 22mil visitors in 10 months, generates RM17.8bil
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Johor attracted 22 million visitors between January and October, marking a 7.5 per cent increase compared with the same period last year, despite regional conflicts, rising fuel prices and haze. Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said 4.7 million overnight visitors were recorded between January and June, comprising 3.3 million domestic tourists and 1.4 million international tourists. "Bangsa Johor will always come first.

items.title: Mersing airport plan hinges on viability study, says Onn Hafiz
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Johor is open to building an airport in Mersing to improve access to its 47 islands, but a comprehensive feasibility study must first establish the project's commercial viability. Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the proposed airport had been identified in the Johor Structure Plan 2030 as part of efforts to improve connectivity to tourism destinations in the district. Mersing's 47 islands and rocky outcrops, including Pulau Rawa, Pulau Besar, Pulau Sibu, Pulau Aur and Pulau Pemanggil, offer significant potential for marine tourism.

items.title: Orkim gets sukuk rating upgrade on stronger PNB backing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MARC Ratings has upgraded the rating of Orkim Bhd's Islamic Medium-Term Notes programme to AAis from AA-is, reflecting stronger shareholder support following Permodalan Nasional Bhd's (PNB) emergence as its majority shareholder. The rating agency also revised the outlook to stable from positive, citing Orkim's strengthened ownership and support profile, alongside its strong standalone credit fundamentals. MARC Ratings said Orkim's standalone credit profile continued to be supported by its leading position in domestic clean petroleum products (CPP) transportation, strong earnings visibility from long-term charters with established oil majors and high barriers to entry.

items.title: Tiger Woods' apparel line loses in trademark appeal
items.summary: Reversing a lower court ruling, the 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals in Pasadena, California, said courts in the state lacked jurisdiction to consider claims by Woods' Sunday Red against Tigeraire, a Louisiana company that makes cooling fans attachable to athletes' headgear. Tuesday's decision does not affect Tigeraire's trademark infringement lawsuit against Sunday Red, which has been put on hold. FIFTEEN STRIPES Sun Day Red, as Woods' brand is known, launched in February 2024, paying homage to Woods wearing red on Sundays during golf tournaments.

items.title: From the CamPro engine to clean energy: How one Khazanah scholar charted Malaysia’s transition
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Before venturing into renewable energy, Syed Malek Faisal Syed Mohamad was part of Proton’s powertrain team, working on the electronic systems that controlled the national carmaker’s engines. His later work in electric mobility eventually led him to help build the renewable energy business at Gentari. Where it began: Proton Syed Malek said he had always been interested in both mechanics and electronics.

items.title: Orphaned Bidayuh student from Lundu chases teaching dream at UPSI thanks to SULUNG aid
items.summary: TANJONG MALIM, Nov 24 — Just a year ago, Grace Ezra Bunad, a young Bidayuh woman from the rural district of Lundu in Sarawak, considered abandoning her dream of going to university after facing financial hardship following the loss of her main source of support. The first in her family to enter higher education, Grace Ezra was among those selected for the SULUNG 4.0 First-Generation Student Development Programme, run by the Ministry of Higher Education (MOHE). Grace Ezra, who hopes to become a Mathematics teacher, said the SULUNG scholarship helped reduce her financial burden by covering her semester tuition fees, along with laboratory, health, and sports charges.

items.title: Underage motorists arrested in KL surge to 114 in first 10 months
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Police detained 114 school students under 17 for reckless and dangerous driving in Kuala Lumpur between January and October this year, up from 69 throughout 2025. Meanwhile, he said the Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department carried out 563,953 enforcement actions in the first 10 months of this year, compared with 444,594 during the same period last year. Fadil said the actions included issuing notices and summonses, as well as seizures and arrests, under five major operations: Op Pematuhan, Op Perdagangan, Op Khas Bersepadu, Op Motosikal and Op Mabuk.

items.title: Women’s Ministry Ministry to engage employers on wider adoption of flexible work arrangements
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry (KPWKM) is ready to negotiate with the private sector to expand Flexible Working Arrangements (FWA), particularly to help women balance career and family responsibilities. Deputy Minister Lim Hui Ying said the ministry would discuss with stakeholders to find solutions balancing employees' interests and employers' operational needs. She said this when winding up the debate on the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027 and the 2027 Development Expenditure Estimates at the committee stage for KPWKM.

items.title: National Laureate A. Samad Said dies, son announces
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — National Laureate Datuk Seri A. Samad Said has died at 91, according to a social media post by his son, musician and writer Az Samad, today. In a Facebook post, Az Samad said his father had passed away and that the family was in the process of making funeral arrangements. “My father passed away and our family is currently arranging funeral details.

items.title: Police to question 25 crew members over actress’ harassment claim
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Police have recorded statements from six individuals to assist in the investigation into allegations that an actress was a victim of sexual harassment by a male actor during the filming of a drama recently. Kuala Lumpur Criminal Investigation Department (CID) Chief SAC Sazalee Adam said that so far, those whose statements have been recorded consist of the complainant, the complainant’s fiancé who is also her personal assistant (PA), the suspect, the director, and two witnesses who are cameramen. Previously, a social media post went viral on social media that the actress had alleged sexual harassment occurred during the filming of a drama.

items.title: Anwar marks four years as PM, vows to continue reforms and ease cost-of-living pressures
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today marked the fourth anniversary of his swearing-in as prime minister, describing the past four years as a challenging period of rebuilding the nation while pledging to continue efforts to strengthen the economy, governance and public welfare. In a Facebook post, Anwar said he still remembered the weight of the responsibility he assumed when he took office amid economic pressures, fiscal constraints and rising living costs faced by Malaysians. Anwar said the Madani Government had over the past four years laid a stronger foundation for Malaysia through efforts to improve the country’s financial position, strengthen governance, advance institutional reforms and enhance support for public welfare.

items.title: Zahid, Tok Mat and Asyraf Wajdi to meet Tuanku Muhriz on Thursday to present BN’s decision on Negeri Sembilan crisis
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 24 — Three top Barisan Nasional (BN) leaders are expected to have an audience with the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, at Istana Hinggap here on Thursday, Sinar Harian reported. Citing a source, the Malay daily said the three are BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, BN deputy chairman and Negeri Sembilan BN chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, and Umno secretary-general Datuk Seri Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki. “The purpose of the audience is to present the party’s decision reached at a special meeting at Wisma Umno Negeri Sembilan last Friday night.

items.title: ‘Busy 12 months ahead’: Hannah Yeoh jokes KL may not have enough weekends in 2027 to accommodate events
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Kuala Lumpur may not have enough weekends next year to accommodate the growing number of events and programmes planned for the capital, Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh joked today. She said the expansion of KL Festival and other creative programmes, supported by the government and private sector, would create more job opportunities while attracting domestic and international visitors. Hannah said the festival’s second edition would run for 25 days, with support from the Federal Territories Ministry, Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and the Finance Ministry, adding that she expected a bigger crowd than this year.

items.title: Hannah says KL’s heritage sites can become international attractions, points to Macron’s visit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Kuala Lumpur’s heritage landmarks have the potential to become international tourist attractions, Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh said, pointing to the positive public response to French President Emmanuel Macron’s recent visit to the capital. She said Macron’s walkabout through the city, including his appearance at Dataran Merdeka with the Sultan Abdul Samad Building as a backdrop, showed how Kuala Lumpur’s historic sites could help shape its appeal to international visitors. “I think that choice says something about how we want the world to see Kuala Lumpur.

items.title: KL Festival to return next year with 25-day programme across Downtown KL
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — KL Festival will return to Downtown Kuala Lumpur from May 6 to 30 next year, with Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh hoping to turn the capital into a more attractive destination through cultural events and unconventional tourism offerings. “I think that what makes Kuala Lumpur important is that it gives people a reason to come back to explore,” Hannah said at the KL Festival 2027 Announcement and Partners’ Reception here today. She said Kuala Lumpur needed to explore new attractions that could appeal to different groups of visitors, including younger tourists, rather than relying solely on conventional sightseeing and shopping experiences.

items.title: State may seek federal loan to resolve drainage problems, says Amirudin
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 24 — The Selangor state government is prepared to obtain a loan from the Federal Government if necessary to accelerate the implementation of flood mitigation projects, including resolving drainage system problems at the local authority level. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the move reflects the state government’s commitment to ensuring that flooding issues, particularly flash floods that frequently occur in urban areas, can be addressed more comprehensively. “Given that the state government currently has no outstanding loans from the Federal Government, I believe that whether the amount is tens of millions or billions of ringgit, I think it is worth it for the state government to take out a loan to resolve these drainage problems, including those at the local authority level,” he said during the winding-up session of the 2027 Development Expenditure Estimates debate at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly sitting today.

items.title: Federal Government remains united despite political differences, says Zahid
items.summary: BALI, Nov 24 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has stressed that differences in political views and positions among parties forming the Federal Government do not affect the country’s administration. Ahmad Zahid, also Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said political maturity enabled party leaders to put aside their differences when carrying out their shared responsibility of governing the country. “When it comes to administering the government, we set aside those differences.

items.title: Malaysians can now renew passports through MyGov Malaysia app
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 24 — Malaysians can now renew their passports through the MyGov Malaysia app, including submitting applications, making online payments and selecting an Immigration Department office for passport collection. In a statement today, the Digital Ministry said the enhanced MyGov Malaysia app version 2.1.4 allows the public to manage applications digitally with greater ease and speed. According to the statement, the facility is among the key improvements introduced by GovTech Malaysia to strengthen the digitalisation of public services.

items.title: Harith Iskander’s lawyers unable to reach him, court defers bid to withdraw from Rosmah suit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Lawyers representing comedian Harith Iskander in a defamation suit brought by Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor have been unable to contact him despite repeated attempts, prompting the High Court today to defer their application to withdraw from the case until December 4. High Court judge Arziah Mohamed Apandi set the new date after Harith failed to attend today’s proceedings, directing his lawyers to make further reasonable efforts to ensure he appeared in person on that date or, at the very least, provided a reasonable response, Utusan Malaysia reported. Lawyer Sangeet Kaur Deo told the court that attempts to serve notice on Harith had been made through email, WhatsApp and visits to his home.

items.title: Perak gets RM40m for road repairs, half earmarked for Tambun and Ipoh, housing minister says
items.summary: IPOH, Nov 24 — The Housing and Local Government Ministry (KPKT) has allocated RM40 million to Perak for road repair and resurfacing works, particularly in residential areas across the state. He said the funds came from the ministry’s cost-saving measures, which had reduced wastage and improved management efficiency, generating total savings of RM67.4 million. Of the savings, the government had decided to prioritise Perak by allocating RM40 million, including RM20 million specifically for the Tambun parliamentary constituency and surrounding areas of Ipoh, which has the highest population density in the state.

items.title: Masidi: Sabah awaits RM900m federal grant ahead of 2027 Budget amid oil revenue uncertainty
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 24 — The Sabah state government is preparing the 2027 Budget by reviewing all expenditure components to ensure they meet the state’s needs and priorities, in line with prudent spending principles. Deputy Chief Minister II and State Finance Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun said he and state officials are detailing every budget item, including basic infrastructure development. Masidi said the additional RM900 million interim grant from the federal government is expected to strengthen the state’s financial position if channelled on time.

items.title: Pakatan sec-gen hails Sarawak’s support for federal government after talks with Abang Johari
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 24 — A meeting between Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail and Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg in Sarawak yesterday focused, among other things, on strengthening cooperation between the federal government and the state. Saifuddin Nasution, who is also Pakatan Harapan secretary-general, said the meeting covered several matters of mutual interest, including security, politics, the economy and public welfare. Mutual respect, understanding and trust must continue to form the foundation of federal-Sarawak relations.

items.title: Melaka warns repeat-offending trishaw riders of licence revocation within 24 hours
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 24 — The Melaka state government is continuing its efforts to enhance the quality of trishaw services through an annual licensing programme to improve the professionalism of trishaw riders while strengthening the state’s image as a tourist destination. State Housing, Local Government and Rural Development Committee chairman Datuk Abdul Razak Abdul Rahman said the initiative also involved improving enforcement to ensure that trishaw riders complied with the stipulated conditions and regulations. The Melaka Historic City Council (MBMB) has been tasked with identifying trishaw riders who repeatedly commit offences, including revoking their licences within 24 hours.

items.title: Political stability tops Saifuddin Nasution’s list of Madani government’s four-year achievements
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Political stability, economic prosperity, public welfare and good governance are the four areas Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail identified as the Madani government’s key achievements over its four years in office. Saifuddin said the administration had managed to maintain political stability, recalling the circumstances surrounding its formation on November 24, 2022. “Firstly, the Madani government has succeeded in establishing political stability.

items.title: Puchong poultry firm, four individuals charged over 6,555kg of chicken allegedly passed off as halal
items.summary: Zafirah Karim, 36; Tanjena Akter Mollah, 35; Hosain Saddam, 34; and Abdul Rahim Ariff Ali, 34 pleaded not guilty before Judge Ainul Bashiirah Dona Don Biyajid after the charges were read to them separately. Abdul Rahim is accused of abetting Syarikat Ayam Segar BM in committing the same offence. The directors, the manager and Abdul Rahim are charged under the same subparagraph, which carries a fine not exceeding RM1 million or imprisonment of up to three years, or both upon conviction.

items.title: Hundreds of millions in idle research funds, missing medical prototypes: PAC flags ‘betrayal of the nation’s trust’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Hundreds of millions of ringgit in public research funds have been left idle, some for nearly two decades, alongside findings of missing medical prototypes and misused development funds, Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC) revealed today, as it warned that systemic governance failures could undermine Malaysia’s technological competitiveness. PAC chairman Datuk Wira Mas Ermieyati Samsudin said the lack of clear refund policies and post-project assessments had left RM183.11 million in unused grant balances unreturned across 11 implementing agencies. The Ministry of Higher Education alone has accumulated more than RM225 million in idle funds over nearly 20 years, the Masjid Tanah MP revealed.

items.title: Drug syndicates changing tactics, Saifuddin Nasution warns of more arrests as enforcement continues
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Drug syndicates may be adapting their methods and strategies, but enforcement agencies are keeping their activities under surveillance, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said today, warning that more arrests would follow. He said Malaysia’s strategic geographical position made it a key location for international drug distribution, requiring enforcement agencies to remain vigilant. Saifuddin said drug trafficking was not the only criminal activity being monitored by enforcement agencies, which were also keeping tabs on telecommunications fraud and online scams.

items.title: Johor Customs intercepts two vessels in RM31.6m cigarette, diesel smuggling crackdown
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 24 — The Customs Department has crippled a cigarette and diesel smuggling syndicate, seizing goods worth a total of RM31.6 million in two separate operations in Johor waters. Johor Customs director Aminul Izmeer Mohd Sohaimi said two vessels and 16 Myanmar crew members, aged between 25 and 53, were also detained in the operations conducted in the waters off Pengerang and Kukup. He said in the first operation, at 11.40am on October 21, a team from the Johor Bahru Customs Enforcement Branch’s Marine Operations Unit detained a vessel in the waters off Pengerang, following intelligence shared by Indonesia’s Directorate General of Customs and Excise (DJBC).

items.title: DPM Zahid: Malaysia eyes Indonesia’s village rating model under new rural development partnership
items.summary: BALI, Nov 24 — Malaysia and Indonesia have agreed to establish a Joint Working Group (JWG) to strengthen cooperation in rural development, including through the exchange of best practices in village management in both countries. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who is currently on a working visit to Indonesia, said Malaysia could benefit from Indonesia’s experience specifically its more structured village rating system to improve data collection and the effectiveness of rural development programme implementation. He added that this rating system could serve as a reference for developing an index or set of standards to measure the level of village development, thereby assisting the government in planning development programmes more effectively.

items.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain forecast across much of Malaysia until 5pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several states and the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and Labuan until 5pm today. Similar weather conditions are also forecast in Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap, Baling, Sik and Kulim in Kedah; Hulu Perak, Selama, Larut Matang, Kuala Kangsar and Kinta in Perak; Jeli, Gua Musang and Kuala Krai in Kelantan; Kuantan, Pekan, Jerantut and Rompin in Pahang; Kuala Langat, Sepang, Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Hulu Langat, Petaling and Klang in Selangor; as well as Mersing and Kota Tinggi in Johor. In Sarawak and Sabah, the affected areas are Mukah (Mukah, Matu, Dalat and Daro), Sibu (Selangau), Bintulu, Miri (Subis, Miri and Marudi), Kuching, Samarahan (Samarahan and Asajaya), Limbang, Sri Aman (Pantu), Serian and Kapit (Song, Bukit Mabong and Kapit); and Kudat, Sandakan, Tawau, the Interior (Membakut, Beaufort, Kuala Penyu and Sipitang) and the West Coast (Ranau and Papar).

items.title: Malaysia must bolster cyber defences as attacks threaten to paralyse government systems, says Saifuddin Nasution
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Cyberattacks targeting critical government systems could paralyse national institutions, underscoring the need for Malaysia to strengthen its security capabilities and preparedness, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said today. He said cyberattacks had emerged as a growing security threat, with incidents in several countries demonstrating how government systems, including taxation, electoral and police databases, could become targets. “We have the National Security Council.

items.title: Malaysia plans to make Year One entry compulsory for six-year-olds from 2029, Education D-G says
items.summary: Education director-general Datuk Mohd Azam Ahmad said the transition would give the Education Ministry time to prepare schools, adapt the curriculum and equip teachers to cater to younger pupils, the New Straits Times reported. As of September 30, the ministry had received 73,498 applications for Year One places from six-year-olds for the 2027 academic year, accounting for nearly 15 per cent of the 491,649 applications received. Speaking at a media briefing, Azam said preparations had begun this year to ensure the policy could be implemented and sustained.

items.title: Pardons Board minutes declassified to help AG prepare affidavit, now public documents, says Saifuddin Nasution
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — The minutes of the Pardons Board meeting were declassified to help the Attorney General (AG) prepare an affidavit in a judicial review brought by the Bar Council, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said today. The minister said he would leave the matter to the IGP. Earlier today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim dismissed accusations in Parliament that the government was responsible for leaking the minutes of the Pardons Board meeting concerning Datuk Seri Najib Razak.

items.title: Five-month-old baby hurt in monkey attack at Sungai Buloh house
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — A five-month-old baby boy sustained facial injuries after a wild monkey attacked him at his home in Kampung Paya Jaras Tengah, Sungai Buloh, last Sunday. Sungai Buloh police chief Supt Mohd Hafiz Muhammad Nor said police received a report regarding the incident at 11.44 pm on the same day. Mohd Hafiz said the victim, the second child of the woman, was taken to Sungai Buloh Hospital for treatment.
